calibrated.why: same rule as the 11.11 baseline: today's forward P/E is undefined (our FY2027 operating margin is -1.4% in the base, so FY2027 operating EPS is negative; FY2027 consensus EPS -6.16, pre-report) and NBIS has no own P/E history (losses since the 2024 relisting); 22 kept = a market-average multiple held for a business still growing ~7% in 2032 (judgement, not an observed NBIS multiple). Holding a sales multiple instead is not credible for a 13%-ROIC, capital-heavy business.

two_lens.rule: lenses disagree: hold, or stage the trade around the next report

price_ladder.method: price today = year-end value at the horizon / (1 + return) ^ years_to_horizon; one return per rung

margin_of_safety_13.label: margin of safety: fixed 13% a year for every company
margin_of_safety_13.meaning: the base case alone at 13% a year
margin_of_safety_13.note: not the margin-of-safety price: that is buy_test.margin_of_safety_price (all four buy-test legs with the base at 13%), never above the buy-test price

buy_test.label: buy test: base return 12% a year

margin_of_safety.label: entry with a margin of safety: buy_return 12% a year
margin_of_safety.note: not the fixed margin of safety: that is the margin_of_safety_13 rung

price_ladder.calibrated_note: the calibrated rungs hold the multiple of today's price (or calibrated.pe) to the horizon; after a price move a rerun holds the new multiple (see buy_test.rerun)

buy_test.rule: base >= 12% a year in both lenses, bull >= 17%, bear >= -10% (yearly returns from today's price to the horizon year-end)
buy_test.no_price_passes: the bear case wipes the equity at the horizon: no price passes that leg
buy_test.margin_of_safety_rule: the buy test with the base at 13% a year in both lenses (bull >= 17%, bear >= -10%): the highest price at which all four legs pass; the rerun price when a rerun at that price holds a lower multiple
buy_test.margin_of_safety_note: the bear case wipes the equity at the horizon: no price passes that leg

dated_values.method: log-linear (geometric) interpolation between today, the base year-end and the dated year-end values, the same rule as forecast_tracker.value_at; return_pct is the yearly rate from today's price to the value on that date
dated_values.note: conditional values on each path at a calendar date, not price forecasts; a wiped scenario is 0 with a null return; beyond_last_year_end_days = the date is after the last modelled year-end and the last year's rate was carried on. the 1-2 year value is the noisiest number here: over one or two years the price follows the multiple and the news far more than the value; the 5-year value rests on the business path

method_gap.note: each method alone, from the same inputs: return = that method's value at the horizon year-end against today's price; dcf_implied_exit_pe = the DCF's value of the business at the horizon (cash taken out) over the next year's after-tax operating profit, to read against the exit P/E. The published value is the plain average of the two; nothing here changes it

sensitivity_terminal.note: the terminal inputs, one changed at a time on the base case: model arithmetic, not a forecast; a null side means the input leaves no terminal value (discount rate or ROIC at or below the growth); at_3pct = terminal growth of 3% instead of the risk-free rate

rows.change: +/- 0.5 point (the model uses the risk-free rate)

return_with_distributions.note: a second line, never the headline: the model leaves each year's free cash in the company at the cash yield, while the index it is compared with reinvests its distributions. Here the cash above today's net cash (above zero for a company in net debt, which repays first) is paid out at each year-end and reinvested at the cost of equity to the horizon; return_with_distributions_at_index_pct reinvests it at the index return instead. Changing the headline needs a preregistered test
